name.text: 16.1 Q4 Classifying a Kisumu school clubs relation

questiontext.text:
At a secondary school in Kisumu, students can join clubs such as drama, football, debate and science. The school keeps a record linking people to clubs.

[[if test="is(sc=1)"]]

Each club has exactly one chairperson, and no student chairs more than one club. In this record the input is a chairperson and the output is the club that he or she chairs.

[[elif test="is(sc=2)"]]

Every student must join exactly one club, and each club has many members. In this record the input is a student and the output is the club that the student belongs to.

[[elif test="is(sc=3)"]]

Each club has exactly one patron, a teacher who looks after it, and every patron looks after several clubs. In this record the input is a patron and the output is a club that the patron looks after.

[[else]]

Students may join as many clubs as they like, and each club has many members. In this record the input is a student and the output is a club that the student belongs to.

[[/if]]

(a) What type of relation is this record?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Is this relation a function?

The relation is [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
To classify a relation, check both directions. First ask how many outputs one input can have. Then ask how many inputs can share one output. The type is named "inputs-to-outputs": many-to-one means many inputs share one output, and one-to-many means one input has many outputs.

[[if test="is(sc=1)"]]

Each chairperson chairs exactly one club, and each club has exactly one chairperson. One input gives one output, and no output is shared, so the relation is one-to-one.

[[elif test="is(sc=2)"]]

Each student belongs to exactly one club, but many students share the same club. Many inputs go to one output, so the relation is many-to-one.

[[elif test="is(sc=3)"]]

Each patron looks after several clubs, but each club has only one patron. One input goes to many outputs, so the relation is one-to-many.

[[else]]

A student can belong to several clubs, and a club has many students. Inputs can have many outputs and outputs can have many inputs, so the relation is many-to-many.

[[/if]]

A relation is a function when each input has exactly one output. So one-to-one and many-to-one relations are functions, while one-to-many and many-to-many relations are not. This relation is therefore {@if sc<=2 then "a function" else "not a function"@}.

questiondescription.text: This question is based on the definitions of one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many relations in Section 16.1 (Types of Relations) of the Grade 11 Functions topic.

feedbackvariables.text: /* Reversal misconception: the student read the record from output to input. */ isrev: is(ans1 = rev);

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="isrev"]]

Check the direction. You seem to have read the record from the club back to the person. The record goes from the input named in the question to the club. Count how many clubs one input is linked to, and how many inputs share one club.

[[else]]

Check both directions before deciding. How many outputs can one input have: one or many? How many inputs can share one output: one or many? The type is named inputs-to-outputs, so many-to-one means many inputs share one output.

[[/if]]

A relation is a function when every input has exactly one output. Decide whether any input in this record can have more than one output. One-to-one and many-to-one relations pass this test; one-to-many and many-to-many relations fail it.

qtest.description: Mixed: type right, function decision wrong
